messages:
maya: Ran an nsys + perfetto trace for the TRT-vLLM wrapper path. Heatmap attached, but quick summary: lots of small kernel launches with ~120-150ms per-request wrapper overhead. Command: `nsys profile -o ttr_vllm_ns --trace=cuda,nvtx python3 perf_runs/run_trt_vllm.py --batch 1`

alex: can you paste the NVTX stack around the slow requests? my hunch is repeated `wrap_invoke` -> `scheduler::dispatch` -> `engine::execute` loops. quick grep you can run: `nsys export -f sqlite ttr_vllm_ns.qdrep | sqlite3 -cmd "select name,dur from nvtx_events limit 50;"`

perf-bot: nsys-summary: total_time=2.73s, cuda_time=1.95s, host_idle=0.48s, memcpy_time=0.05s, kernel_launch_overhead_est=0.21s

jordan: +1 on NVTX. also check if KV cache warmup is triggering syncs. I saw `kv_cache->ensure_ready()` in the trace right before dispatch which stalls for ~40ms on some requests. that lines up with the warmup hypothesis. :thinking:

sam: try toggling batching heuristics: set env `REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_BATCH=8` and `REDWOOD_BATCHER_WAIT_MS=5` and re-run. also run with `REDWOOD_KV_WARMUP=0` to force cold vs warm comparisons. I suspect the scheduler busy-waits when KV isn't warm.

maya: repro steps I used: `python3 perf_runs/run_trt_vllm.py --model gpt-small --requests 100 --pipelined` then `nsys profile ...` I captured NVTX markers from wrapper with this pattern: `NVTX_PUSH(\"wrap:invoke:request_id=%d\")` at entry and `NVTX_POP()` at exit. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/#/view?trace=ttr_vllm_ns (internal)

alex: can you dump a short textual slice from the perfetto capture? what I'm looking for is the gap between `wrap:invoke` NVTX and first kernel start. If that gap is host-side scheduling + memcpy + KV checks, it points at scheduler + kv path. example line I'd expect: `wrap:invoke [0ms-150ms] -> scheduler::dispatch [5ms-30ms] -> Engine::infer kernel_launch [30ms-145ms]`

maya: pasted a small slice below (from the nsys exported CSV):
```
event, start_ms, end_ms
wrap:invoke, 0.0, 148.7
scheduler::dispatch, 6.2, 28.9
kv_cache::ensure_ready, 7.5, 49.9
Engine::infer, 31.0, 145.3
cudaKernel:attention_k, 32.1, 78.2
cudaKernel:softmax_k, 80.0, 111.4
cudaKernel:gelu_k, 112.0, 142.9
```

jordan: that `kv_cache::ensure_ready` jump to ~50ms is suspicious — why is it that long? maybe we deserialize some metadata on first access or there is a lock. grep for `std::mutex` on KV path. another idea: if wrapper holds the scheduler mutex while waiting on KV, it will block concurrent batches.

sam: also consider enabling CUDA graphs for the engine path, if Engine::infer is captured with graphs you should see kernel launch collapsing. if graphs are off, you pay the per-launch overhead. set `TRT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPHS=1`. in my local it dropped Engine::infer from 110ms to ~40ms. :rocket:

alex: small reproducible test: run two modes back-to-back: (A) `REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_BATCH=1 TR...` and (B) `REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_BATCH=8` and compare `nvprof` kernel launch counts. if you see many more launches in A, batching logic isn't coalescing. also compare `nsys` host CPU stacks to see scheduler hot functions.

maya: ran the two-mode diff. Results: mode A (batch1) had 97 kernel launches / 100 requests. mode B had 18 kernel launches / 100 requests. unexpected part: wrapper overhead per-request only reduced from 150ms -> 110ms with batching enabled; still ~80ms unaccounted host time.

perf-bot: quick flame summary: top host frames: `wrapper::invoke_loop` 32%, `scheduler::poll` 18%, `kv_cache::lock_and_load` 12%, `engine::enqueue_and_launch` 22%

jordan: that points to active polling. can you enable the scheduler sleep-yield path? there's a compile switch `SCHED_POLL_BACKOFF_MS` default 0. set to 1 or 2 to reduce busy spin. it may add a few ms but free CPU and reduce latency variance.

sam: another angle: instrumentation overhead. NVTX + nsys add measurement overhead — try a minimal run without NVTX on the hot path and compare. also check if `std::chrono::high_resolution_clock` calls are frequent in hot loop. use `perf record -e cycles:u -g --pid=...` host-side to get call stacks without CUDA overhead.

maya: good points. next actions I'm going to run: 1) rerun with KV warmup disabled to force cache warmed path, 2) toggle `SCHED_POLL_BACKOFF_MS=2`, 3) enable CUDA graphs, 4) redo nsys with minimal NVTX. I'll attach the perf record stack and short perfetto slice when done. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

alex: SGTM. if graphs + batch + backoff still leaves >40ms host overhead, we should instrument wrapper to time `serialize_request` vs `route_to_scheduler` vs `post_to_engine` with microtimers and dump to metrics. that will tell us if it's serialization or scheduling.

maya: noted. I'll run those and post results in this thread in ~30m.

sam: ping me when the perf-record is up, I can decode stacks and map to source lines.

maya: will do — uploading first artifacts now (nsys qdrep + exported CSV).
